summary:
We developed an interactive educational web game designed to introduce users of all ages to the forgotten expeditions, spacecraft, and equipment that shaped modern space exploration. Starting from Earth’s orbit and progressing across different celestial bodies, players explore themed modules featuring accessible, bite-sized theory lessons followed by interactive quizzes to reinforce their knowledge.
Our project directly addresses the challenge by highlighting overlooked NASA missions and technologies that remain on distant worlds—crucial milestones that paved the way for today’s achievements but are largely unknown to the general public and younger generations.
This is important because as humanity looks toward ambitious goals like Mars colonization, understanding the history and foundational tools behind spaceflight prevents knowledge gaps and fosters deeper scientific curiosity. By turning NASA’s hidden history into an engaging game, we make space education accessible, memorable, and inspiring for everyone.
details:
How It Works

Our project is an interactive, browser-based educational game structured like a space journey. When users land on the homepage and click the "Start" button, they enter a progressive learning map divided into planetary sections, beginning with Earth’s Orbit. Each section contains five themed topics dedicated to overlooked NASA expeditions, spacecraft, and instruments that remain on distant celestial bodies. Within each topic, players follow a clear learning loop: first, they read a short, easy-to-understand theory card about a specific space object (such as an early satellite or lander), and then they complete an interactive quiz to test and reinforce what they have learned before advancing further.

Benefits & Intended Impact

The platform makes complex aerospace history engaging, structured, and accessible to learners of all ages. As modern space initiatives—such as planned missions to Mars—capture global attention, many people lack foundational knowledge about the pioneering missions that made current progress possible. Our project bridges this gap, broadens public awareness of NASA’s full historical legacy, and prevents common misconceptions by showing the step-by-step engineering breakthroughs behind space exploration.

Creativity

Instead of presenting space history as a static encyclopedia or dry textbook, we gamified NASA’s lesser-known archives. By focusing specifically on the "forgotten" hardware left behind on other worlds and turning each mission into a bite-sized interactive level, we give unsung technological heroes the spotlight they deserve.

Tools & Technologies Used

To build this web application, we used core web technologies—HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript—leveraging AI-assisted development (OpenAI Codex) and prompt engineering to generate, structure, and refine the codebase. For educational accuracy, we relied on official NASA open data, mission archives, and historical documentation as our primary information sources.
